one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events probably fall in the window. (1) Q3 2026 results, estimated for Oct 26 after the close. The date is not company-confirmed: as of Oct 1 there is no Cadence Q3 webcast notice. Last year's Q3 notice came out on Oct 3, 2025, and the Q2 2026 notice on Jul 6, about three weeks ahead (sources 28, 30), so a late-October report inside the window is still very likely. Guidance is revenue of $1.595-1.625B and non-GAAP EPS of $2.01-2.07 (source 2). Consensus is $1.612B and $2.05 (source 27), right at the guide midpoint. Cadence beat the top of its EPS range in Q2. The FY26 EPS guide went from $8.05-8.15 (Feb, ex-Hexagon) to $7.85-7.95 (Q1, with Hexagon) and back to $8.05-8.15 (Q2), so organic beats are absorbing the Hexagon dilution (sources 4, 2). That points to a beat and a small raise as the modal outcome. (2) The Oct 28 FOMC: the supervisor verified ~26% odds of a hike, and the 10-year is at 5.29% (source 29). The September 19% drawdown to $273.96 came with no company news, which shows rates can move this multiple sharply within weeks. The stock is up 28% in 12 sessions, so short-term reversal risk roughly cancels the beat-and-raise drift. Synopsys's August reaction (+13% the next day, then -21% by Sep 15, per the supervisor's check) shows a beat is rewarded on the day but gives no protection against a rate-driven move. No directional edge, so I use a symmetric lognormal with a median of ~$351 and a 1-month sigma of ~12.7%. That is slightly above annual vol / 3.5 (11.7%) to cover the earnings gap plus the FOMC; it is a touch wider than round 1 for the FOMC.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 $10.60 x 35x = $371) + 40% FCF yield (NTM FCF $2.33B at 2.5% = $93.3B, less ~$0.4B net debt, / 276M shares = $337) = ~$357. Down from $375 because I now use a correct NTM basis instead of FY2028 alone, and I raised the net-debt assumption.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at 2027-10-01 of $10.60 (0.25 x FY2027E $9.55 + 0.75 x FY2028E $10.90) x 35x forward multiple

inputs_detail.derivation: Guide path: $8.05-8.15 (Feb, ex-Hexagon, source 15), then $7.85-7.95 (Q1, including Hexagon dilution, source 4), then $8.05-8.15 (Q2, raised $0.20, source 2). Consensus is $8.14 (source 27).

StockAnalysis has $9.56 from 26 analysts (S&P Global) and Zacks has $9.43 (sources 27, 10). My bottom-up check gives ~$9.45-9.55: $7.17B revenue x ~45% non-GAAP margin, less ~$0.1B other expense, a 16.5% tax rate (source 2) and 276M shares.

FY2027 $9.55 grown ~14%: revenue +12% and a ~1pt margin gain, with flat shares. Support: 58% of RPO converts within 12 months and next-12-month RPO grew from $3.8B to $4.2B in H1 2026 (sources 3, 2). Synopsys guides FY27 +15% with a 13%+ long-term EDA CAGR (source 21). The supervisor uses ~$11.0; I stay slightly below it because Cadence guides conservatively.
0.25 x $9.55 + 0.75 x $10.90 = $10.56, rounded to $10.60. This replaces round 1, where I used FY2028E $10.90 alone as NTM. The supervisor flagged that error and I accept it.
FY26 guide 275.5-277.5M. Buybacks of ~0.58-0.67M shares a quarter ($200M a quarter, source 2) roughly offset SBC issuance, so I hold the count flat.

Today $350.73 is ~38x NTM EPS ($9.21 = 0.25 x 8.14 + 0.75 x 9.56) and ~36.7x FY27; the 5-year forward average is ~45x (source 11). I assume ~3 turns of compression by Oct-2027 because EPS growth slows from ~17% to ~14% and the 10-year sits at 5.29% (source 29). The Sep-15 low of ~30x NTM came with no company news (source 22) and marks the rate-stress floor. Synopsys trades at ~25x its FY27 guide (~28x consensus), but it is post-Ansys, more levered and lower-margin, and Cadence has long carried a premium. So I use 35x rather than the supervisor's 34x; at 34x the leg would be $360.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF at Oct-2027 of $2.33B (0.25 x FY27E $2.11B + 0.75 x FY28E $2.41B) / 2.5% = $93.3B; less net debt ~$0.4B; / 276M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 2026: $2.50B principal less $1.44B cash = $1.06B. Over ~5 quarters FCF is ~$2.2B; ~50% goes to buybacks (~$200M a quarter, source 2), leaving ~$1.1B. I haircut that to ~$0.65B of net reduction for vesting-tax withholding and Cadence's habitual tuck-in M&A (the Q2 commentary still lists 'pending acquisitions' as a risk). Q1-to-Q2 cash rose only $33M despite $635M OCF, because $425M of debt was repaid. Net debt ends ~$0.4B: between my round-1 ~$0 and the supervisor's $0.5-1.0B.
At $350.73 (~$97B market cap) the yield on FY27E FCF is ~2.2%. I use 2.5% on NTM FCF to allow for SBC (H1 SBC $285M, source 3) and a 5.29% 10-year (source 29).

bear.story: The Feb-2027 initial FY27 guide lands near ~10% growth: Cadence guided FY26 initially at 11-13%, then had to cut EPS to absorb Hexagon in Q1 (sources 15, 4). Or the AI-agent and open-source narrative returns. Or the Affiliates Rule restarts after the Jan 10, 2027 truce expiry (China 15% of Q2 revenue). The 10-year stays above 5%. NTM EPS ~$9.9 at ~24x, below the Sept-15 trough multiple and near Synopsys's discount level.

base.story: Beat-and-raise continues. FY27 is guided ~11-12% and ends ~13%, backlog stays above $8B, and margins rebuild once Hexagon integration costs fall away. NTM EPS ~$10.6 at ~35x.

bull.story: Agent consumption pricing shows up in bookings, IP stays at 30%+ growth, hardware stays supply-constrained, and EDA peer guidance (Synopsys FY27 +15%) re-rates the group as yields ease. NTM EPS ~$11.0 at ~43x, near the 5-year average.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$245, about 7% under the $262.75 52-week low and 11% under the $273.96 no-news Sept-15 close. That is ~23x NTM EPS at the horizon ($10.60), below even Synopsys's ~25x on its FY27 guide. At that price the market would be pricing a fundamental reset rather than rates or sentiment: an FY27 guide well under ~10-11% growth, backlog falling from $8.1B, evidence that agents compress license pricing, or loss of China access when the Affiliates Rule suspension ends on Jan 10, 2027. I lower it from $250 because the 23x-NTM floor computed on the corrected EPS basis comes out at ~$244.

reasoning: Round 2. I accept the supervisor's three findings on my work and checked each one. (1) EPS basis: I had capitalized FY2028E EPS as if it were NTM at the horizon. The correct NTM at Oct-2027 is 0.25 x FY27 + 0.75 x FY28 = ~$10.60. I confirmed FY27 consensus of $9.56 (26 analysts) and FY26 of $8.14 on StockAnalysis (source 27). FY28 consensus is paywalled, so I keep my own $10.90. (2) FY26 EPS guide history: confirmed in the Q2 CFO commentary's previous/current table (source 2). Q1 cut the guide to $7.85-7.95 to include Hexagon, and Q2 raised it back to $8.05-8.15. So organic beats recovered the Hexagon dilution within a year, which is a little better than my round-1 claim that it was 'never raised'. (3) Net debt: Q2 net debt is $1.06B, and Q2 cash barely rose because $425M of debt was repaid (source 2). Allowing for buybacks at ~50% of FCF plus tuck-in M&A and withholding, I now use ~$0.4B at the horizon instead of ~$0. I keep 35x rather than the supervisor's suggested 34x. Today's NTM multiple is ~38x; I take 3 turns off for slower growth and 5.29% yields (supervisor-verified H.15, source 29). Synopsys at ~25x guided FY27 is not a clean comp, since it is post-Ansys, more levered and lower-margin. Fair value: P/E $371 (60%) and FCF yield $337 (40%) give $357, down from $375. Scenarios: $235 / $370 / $475 at 23/52/25, mean ~$365. For the ladder I use a mixture: 93% lognormal with median $368 and sigma 0.33, plus a 7% disruption/derating tail with median $240 and sigma 0.40. That gives P(>=351) = 0.53, down from 0.558. The upper strikes (K>=421) come down by ~3pts each, which answers the supervisor's point that mine were the highest of the five. Sigma stays below the 41% realized vol, which includes two narrative shocks; the left-tail component covers those. The 1-month ladder stays near-symmetric around spot, slightly wider for the FOMC. The Q3 date is treated as an estimate (no webcast notice yet; last year's came Oct 3). Research for this round: re-pulled the Q2 CFO commentary from sec.gov, fetched StockAnalysis consensus, ran web searches for the Q3 webcast notice and Synopsys's forward multiple, and took the rates and Polymarket figures from the supervisor's verified evidence. No option data was consulted, and nothing under valuation/priors/ or round1_capped/ was opened.
